title: A Recipe for the Semester
premise: Yara Ishikawa transfers to Aldercrest Academy, a school built atop the ruins of a 19th-century culinary commune whose founders' 'Founders' Feast' tradition still feeds the town every solstice. When a college essay forces her to answer 'What did you survive, and what did it cost?', her honest response accidentally exposes that the Feast's endowment is nearly bankrupt and the town's founders' descendants have been quietly cannibalizing it for generations. Yara, who learned cooking from her late grandmother's recipes as her only inheritance, must rebuild the Feast from scratch with a ragtag kitchen crew, confronting the wealthy family whose survival was bought by the commune's erasure. In the end, the Feast succeeds only because Yara stops hiding her grief and heritage, and the town chooses to fund a tradition that belongs to everyone, not just those who inherited it by theft.
about_author: Orsen Sterling is a former line cook who spent six years in kitchens across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction full-time. They write young adult stories about food, grief, and the strange inheritances families leave in recipe cards.

chapters.title: The New Kid Eats Alone
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Three weeks into Aldercrest Academy, Yara maps the cafeteria's social geography and eats in the library, guarding the secret of her grandmother's recipe box. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Question on the Common App
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. English teacher Mr. Okafor assigns a college essay: 'What did you survive, and what did it cost?' Yara freezes, unable to write a safe, empty answer. Emotional beat: dread of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Founders' Feast Flyer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Volunteering for community service hours, Yara is assigned to the committee planning the 150th Founders' Feast, where she meets Theo Vance, heir to the Vance family that 'saved' the school. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At home, Yara opens the recipe box she hasn't touched since her grandmother's death and finds a card referencing 'Aldercrest Commune, Table Seven.' Emotional beat: grief cracking open into mystery.

chapters.title: Archives Under the Gym
chapters.summary: Yara and Theo's POV, alternating. They sneak into the school's basement archives and discover the Academy was built directly over the commune's original dining hall. Emotional beat: thrill of shared conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds the Feast's financial ledger and realizes his family's trust has been draining the endowment for decades. He hides it from Yara. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: First Honest Draft
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara writes one raw paragraph about her grandmother and immediately deletes it, but Mr. Okafor saw it in the shared doc and asks her to keep going. Emotional beat: terror and relief braided together.

chapters.title: Table Seven
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the recipe card, Yara locates descendants of commune members living at the town's edge, including elderly Marta, who remembers the last true Feast. Emotional beat: finding a lineage she thought was lost.

chapters.title: The Vance Version
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a family dinner, Theo's father rehearses the official founding myth, and Theo hears how many details are lies. Emotional beat: complicity turning to resistance.

chapters.title: Kitchen Crew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara recruits misfits—Marta, cafeteria worker Dee, and quiet sophomore Priya—to test the original commune recipes for a 'historical exhibit' at the Feast. Emotional beat: belonging forming around a worktable.

chapters.title: Burnt First Batch
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crew's first attempt at the communal bread fails spectacularly; Yara's perfectionism nearly ends the project. Priya calls her out. Emotional beat: pride meeting its limit.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara discovers the ledger's missing pages and realizes Theo's family caused the shortfall. She confronts him; he confesses everything. Emotional beat: betrayal and the cost of trust.

chapters.title: The Essay Due Date
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Mr. Okafor returns her draft with one note: 'You survived. Now say what it cost.' Yara writes the truth about her grandmother and her own invisibility. Emotional beat: the essay as confession.

chapters.title: Deadline on the Endowment
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The trust's trustees announce the Feast will be discontinued unless the endowment is privately funded within six weeks. Theo's father expects Theo to sign the closure order. Emotional beat: pressure of inheritance.

chapters.title: Marta's Story
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Marta reveals the commune collapsed because the Vances bought its debt during a hard winter, then rewrote history. The recipes were the members' only surviving property. Emotional beat: anger as inheritance.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: Yara and Theo's POV. They publish the essay, the ledger, and Marta's testimony in the school paper. The town splits; Yara's scholarship is quietly threatened. Emotional beat: the price of speaking.

chapters.title: Empty Seats
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sponsors withdraw, volunteers quit, and the Feast venue is revoked. The crew nearly disbands; Dee offers her diner as a last resort. Emotional beat: despair before the climb.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Prep
chapters.summary: Full crew POV, braided. On solstice eve, the crew cooks through the night in the diner, the whole town smelling the bread and drifting in to help. Emotional beat: a community remembering itself.

chapters.title: Feast of the Founders
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Feast happens in the diner and spills into the streets; Theo publicly renounces his inheritance claim and proposes a town-held trust. Emotional beat: the tradition reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Theo and Yara's POV. Mr. Vance threatens legal action and Yara's enrollment, but the town council, moved by the turnout, votes to charter the Feast as public heritage. Emotional beat: collective power over private wealth.

chapters.title: What It Cost
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reads her final essay aloud at a school assembly—about her grandmother, her silence, and the price of survival—and receives her first acceptance letter. Emotional beat: being seen and surviving it.

chapters.title: Table Seven, Set for Everyone
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, one year later. The Feast is annual and town-funded; Yara adds her own recipe card to the box, beside her grandmother's, and passes it to a new kid eating alone. Emotional beat: inheritance renewed, belonging chosen.
